title: Django REST Framework: serializers and viewsets

videos.script: agenda has pages for people. Today it gets an API, for programs. A phone app, a JavaScript front end, another team's service. {{programs}} Lesson 2 answered JSON with one function. That does not survive contact with real clients. They send broken JSON. They send the wrong types. They need to know why a request failed. {{jobs}} Django REST Framework takes those jobs off your hands. The center of it is the serializer. One class that turns an event into JSON on the way out, and checks JSON before it becomes anything on the way in. {{serializer}} A viewset gives the events five views in one class, and a router writes their URLs. Reading is open. Writing needs a user. {{viewset}} Then registering through the API. It calls the same service as the form, so the lock from lesson 4 protects it too. And every refusal gets the status code that says what happened. 400 for bad data. 409 when the event is full. {{codes}} Last, pagination. A list that returns every row works with three events, and fails with thirty thousand.
